subject.title: [Feature]: Cron job output routing — hard-coded destination for job results (file, channel, session)

question: Should OpenClaw add first-class cron output targets, and what product/security rules should govern file writes, channel fan-out, session injection, silent discard, fallback, and run-status reporting?
rationale: The source gap is high confidence, but the requested feature gives scheduled jobs new framework-owned authority over files, channels, and sessions, which automation should not design without maintainer intent.

options.title: Design one output contract
options.body: Define a single cron output target API with explicit authorization, path policy, delivery semantics, docs, protocol support, and regression tests before implementation.

options.title: Narrow to delivery defaults
options.body: Defer file and session targets and solve only the focused default-recipient problem tracked by https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/9155.

options.title: Reject core output targets
options.body: Keep cron routing prompt/tool-driven or plugin-owned and improve diagnostics or docs instead of adding new core delivery authority.

recommendation.title: Design one output contract
recommendation.body: Define a single cron output target API with explicit authorization, path policy, delivery semantics, docs, protocol support, and regression tests before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest visible routing signal from current blame, older cron default work, and prior triage on this cron delivery cluster.
